## **21.1 Overview**

Choropleth mapping involves the symbolisation of enumeration units, such as countries, provinces, states, counties or census units, using area patterns or graduated colors.

## **21.2 Getting Started**

How to plot functional and truthful choropleth maps by using an R package called [**tmap**](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/tmap/) package. Beside **tmap** package, four other R packages will be used. They are:

-   [**readr**](https://readr.tidyverse.org/) for importing delimited text file,

-   [**tidyr**](https://tidyr.tidyverse.org/) for tidying data,

-   [**dplyr**](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/) for wrangling data and

-   [**sf**](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sf/index.html) for handling geospatial data.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pacman::p_load(sf, tmap, tidyverse)
```
:::

### **21.3.3 Importing Attribute Data into R**

Next, we will import *respopagsex2011to2020.csv* file into RStudio and save the file into an R dataframe called *popagsex*.

The task will be performed by using *read_csv()* function of **readr** package as shown in the code chunk below.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
popdata <- read_csv("data/aspatial/respopagesextod2011to2020.csv")
```
:::



### **21.3.4 Data Preparation**

**Before a thematic map can be prepared, we need to prepare a data table with year 2020 values**. The data table should include the variables PA, SZ, YOUNG, ECONOMY ACTIVE, AGED, TOTAL, DEPENDENCY.

-   YOUNG: age group 0 to 4 until age groyup 20 to 24,

-   ECONOMY ACTIVE: age group 25-29 until age group 60-64,

-   AGED: age group 65 and above,

-   TOTAL: all age group, and

-   DEPENDENCY: the ratio between young and aged against economy active group

#### 21.3.4.1 Data wrangling

The following data wrangling and transformation functions will be used:

-   *pivot_wider()* of **tidyr** package, and

-   *mutate()*, *filter()*, *group_by()* and *select()* of **dplyr** package



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
popdata2020 <- popdata %>%
  filter(Time == 2020) %>%
  group_by(PA, SZ, AG) %>%
  summarise(`POP` = sum(`Pop`)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from=AG, 
              values_from=POP) %>%
  mutate(YOUNG = rowSums(.[3:6])
         +rowSums(.[12])) %>%
mutate(`ECONOMY ACTIVE` = rowSums(.[7:11])+
rowSums(.[13:15]))%>%
mutate(`AGED`=rowSums(.[16:21])) %>%
mutate(`TOTAL`=rowSums(.[3:21])) %>%  
mutate(`DEPENDENCY` = (`YOUNG` + `AGED`)
/`ECONOMY ACTIVE`) %>%
  select(`PA`, `SZ`, `YOUNG`, 
       `ECONOMY ACTIVE`, `AGED`, 
       `TOTAL`, `DEPENDENCY`)
```
:::



#### 21.3.4.2 Joining the attribute data and geospatial data

Before we can perform the georelational join, *one extra step* is required to convert the values in PA and SZ fields to uppercase. This is because the values of PA and SZ fields are made up of upper- and lowercase. On the other, hand the SUBZONE_N and PLN_AREA_N are in uppercase.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
popdata2020 <- popdata2020 %>%
  mutate_at(.vars = vars(PA, SZ), 
          .funs = funs(toupper)) %>%
  filter(`ECONOMY ACTIVE` > 0)
```
:::



Next, *left_join()* of **dplyr** is used to join the geographical data and attribute table using planning subzone name e.g. *SUBZONE_N* and *SZ* as the common identifier.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
mpsz_pop2020 <- left_join(mpsz, popdata2020,
                          by = c("SUBZONE_N" = "SZ"))
```
:::



Thing to learn from the code chunk above:

-   *left_join()* of **dplyr** package is used with `mpsz` simple feature data frame as the left data table is to ensure that the output will be a simple features data frame.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
write_rds(mpsz_pop2020, "data/rds/mpszpop2020.rds")
```
:::



## **21.4 Choropleth Mapping Geospatial Data Using *tmap***

Two approaches can be used to prepare thematic map using *tmap*, they are:

1.  Plotting a thematic map quickly by using *qtm()*.

2.  Plotting highly customisable thematic map by using tmap elements.

### **21.4.1 Plotting a choropleth map quickly by using *qtm()***

The easiest and quickest to draw a choropleth map using **tmap** is using *qtm()*.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tmap_mode("plot")
qtm(mpsz_pop2020, 
    fill = "DEPENDENCY")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-9-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



hings to learn from the code chunk above:

-   *tmap_mode()* with “plot” option is used to produce a static map. For interactive mode, “view” option should be used.

-   *fill* argument is used to map the attribute (i.e. DEPENDENCY)

### **21.4.2 Creating a choropleth map by using *tmap*’s elements**

To draw a high quality cartographic choropleth map as shown in the figure below, **tmap**’s drawing elements should be used.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+
  tm_fill("DEPENDENCY", 
          style = "quantile", 
          palette = "Blues",
          title = "Dependency ratio") +
  tm_layout(main.title = "Distribution of Dependency Ratio by planning subzone",
            main.title.position = "center",
            main.title.size = 1.2,
            legend.height = 0.45, 
            legend.width = 0.35,
            frame = TRUE) +
  tm_borders(alpha = 0.5) +
  tm_compass(type="8star", size = 2) +
  tm_scale_bar() +
  tm_grid(alpha =0.2) +
  tm_credits("Source: Planning Sub-zone boundary from Urban Redevelopment Authorithy (URA)\n and Population data from Department of Statistics DOS", 
             position = c("left", "bottom"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



#### 21.4.2.1 Drawing a base map

The basic building block of **tmap** is *tm_shape()* followed by one or more layer elemments such as *tm_fill()* and *tm_polygons()*.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020) +
  tm_polygons()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



#### 21.4.2.2 Drawing a choropleth map using *tm_polygons()*

we just need to assign the target variable such as *Dependency* to *tm_polygons()*.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+
  tm_polygons("DEPENDENCY")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



#### 21.4.2.3 Drawing a choropleth map using *tm_fill()* and \*tm_border()\*\*

Actually, *tm_polygons()* is a wraper of *tm_fill()* and *tm_border()*. *tm_fill()* shades the polygons by using the default colour scheme and *tm_borders()* adds the borders of the shapefile onto the choropleth map.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+
  tm_fill("DEPENDENCY")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



To add the boundary of the planning subzones

tm_fill("DEPENDENCY") 最後放



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+
  tm_borders(lwd = 0.5, col = "black", alpha = 1)+
  tm_fill("DEPENDENCY")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



### **21.4.3 Data classification methods of tmap**

#### 21.4.3.1 Plotting choropleth maps with built-in classification methods

used 5 classes：



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+
  tm_fill("DEPENDENCY",
          n = 5,
          style = "jenks") +
  tm_borders(alpha = 0.5)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-15-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



In the code chunk below, *equal* data classification method is used.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+
  tm_fill("DEPENDENCY",
          n = 5,
          style = "equal") +
  tm_borders(alpha = 0.5)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-16-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



#### 21.4.3.2 Plotting choropleth map with custome break



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
summary(mpsz_pop2020$DEPENDENCY)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
   Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max.    NA's 
 0.1111  0.7147  0.7866  0.8585  0.8763 19.0000      92 
```


:::
:::



With reference to the results above, we set break point at 0.60, 0.70, 0.80, and 0.90.

Our *breaks* vector is thus c(0, 0.60, 0.70, 0.80, 0.90, 1.00)



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+
  tm_borders(alpha = 0.5)+
  tm_fill("DEPENDENCY",
          breaks = c(0, 0.60, 0.70, 0.80, 0.90, 1.00))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-18-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



### **21.4.4 Colour Scheme**

**tmap** supports colour ramps either defined by the user or a set of predefined colour ramps from the **RColorBrewer** package.

### \*\* \*\*21.4.4.1 Using ColourBrewer palette



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+
  tm_borders(alpha = 0.5)+
  tm_fill("DEPENDENCY",
          n = 6,
          style = "quantile",
          palette = "Blues") 
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-19-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



Notice that the choropleth map is shaded in green.

To reverse the colour shading, add a “-” prefix.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+
  tm_borders(alpha = 0.5)+
  tm_fill("DEPENDENCY",
          style = "quantile",
          palette = "-Greens") 
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-20-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



the colour scheme has been reversed.

### **21.4.5 Map Layouts**

Map layout refers to the combination of all map elements into a cohensive map.

#### 21.4.5.1 Map Legend

In **tmap**, several *legend* options are provided to change the placement, format and appearance of the legend.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+
  
  tm_layout(main.title = "Distribution of Dependency Ratio by planning subzone \n(Jenks classification)",
            main.title.position = "center",
            main.title.size = 1,
            legend.height = 0.45, 
            legend.width = 0.35,
            legend.outside = FALSE,
            legend.position = c("right", "bottom"),
            frame = FALSE) +
  tm_borders(alpha = 0.5) +
  tm_fill("DEPENDENCY", 
          style = "jenks", 
          palette = "Blues", 
          legend.hist = TRUE, 
          legend.is.portrait = TRUE,
          legend.hist.z = 0.1) 
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-21-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



#### 21.4.5.2 Map style

**tmap** allows a wide variety of layout settings to be changed. They can be called by using *tmap_style()*.

The code chunk below shows the *classic* style is used.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+
  tm_borders(alpha = 0.5)+
  tmap_style("classic")+
  tm_fill("DEPENDENCY", 
          style = "quantile", 
          palette = "-Greens")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-22-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



#### 21.4.5.3 Cartographic Furniture



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+
  tm_layout(main.title = "Distribution of Dependency Ratio \nby planning subzone",
            main.title.position = "center",
            main.title.size = 1.2,
            legend.height = 0.45, 
            legend.width = 0.35,
            frame = TRUE) +
  tm_borders(alpha = 0.5)+
  tm_compass(type="8star", size = 2) +
  tm_grid(lwd = 0.1, alpha = 0.2) +
  tm_fill("DEPENDENCY", 
          style = "quantile", 
          palette = "Blues",
          title = "No. of persons") +
  tm_scale_bar()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-23-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tmap_style("white")
```
:::



### **21.4.6 Drawing Small Multiple Choropleth Maps**

**Small multiple maps**, also referred to as **facet maps**, are composed of many maps arrange side-by-side, and sometimes stacked vertically.

#### 21.4.6.1 By assigning multiple values to at least one of the aesthetic arguments

In this example, small multiple choropleth maps are created by defining ***ncols*** in **tm_fill()**



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+
  tm_layout(legend.position = c("right", "bottom")) +
  tm_borders(alpha = 0.5) +
  tm_fill(c("YOUNG", "AGED"),
          style = "equal", 
          palette = "Blues") +
  tmap_style("white")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-25-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



In this example, small multiple choropleth maps are created by assigning multiple values to at least one of the aesthetic arguments



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+ 
  tm_layout(legend.position = c("right", "bottom"))+
  tm_polygons(c("DEPENDENCY","AGED"),
          style = c("equal", "quantile"), 
          palette = list("Blues","Greens")) 
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-26-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::



#### 21.4.6.2 By defining a group-by variable in *tm_facets()*

In this example, multiple small choropleth maps are created by using **tm_facets()**.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
sum(is.na(mpsz_pop2020$REGION_N))  # 查看 NA 的數量
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 0
```


:::
:::

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020) +
  tm_fill("DEPENDENCY",
          style = "quantile",
          palette = "Blues",
          thres.poly = 0) + 
  tm_facets(by = "REGION_N", 
            free.coords = FALSE, 
            drop.shapes = TRUE)

  tm_layout(legend.show = FALSE,
            title.position = c("center", "center"), 
            title.size = 20) +
  tm_borders(alpha = 0.5)
```
:::



#### 21.4.6.3 By creating multiple stand-alone maps with *tmap_arrange()*

In this example, multiple small choropleth maps are created by creating multiple stand-alone maps with **tmap_arrange()**.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
youngmap <- tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+ 
  tm_polygons("YOUNG", 
              style = "quantile", 
              palette = "Blues")

agedmap <- tm_shape(mpsz_pop2020)+ 
  tm_polygons("AGED", 
              style = "quantile", 
              palette = "Blues")

tmap_arrange(youngmap, agedmap, asp=1, ncol=2)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](Handson_Ex08_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-29-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
            legend.position = c("right", "bottom"),

  tm_fill("DEPENDENCY", 
          style = "quantile", 
          palette = "Blues", 
          legend.hist = TRUE, 
          legend.is.portrait = TRUE,
          legend.hist.z = 0.1) 
```
